title: Rav Nachman bar Abba
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Avodah Zarah 39a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.39a.2) has Rav Nachman bar Abba speaking in Rav’s name, but Hyman reports that the Rif and Rosh read Rav Chanan bar Rava.

In [Kiddushin 33a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.33a.18), Rav Nachman says: “Were it not for Torah, how many Nachman bar Abbas would be in the marketplace!” Hyman observes that bar Abba is absent from [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Kiddushin.33a.18.3) and from Dikdukei Soferim, as noted at Megillah 23a, note samekh. He also reports its absence from [Responsa Tashbetz 1:147](https://he.wikisource.org/wiki/%D7%A9%D7%95%22%D7%AA_%D7%A8%D7%A9%D7%91%22%D7%A5_(%D7%AA%D7%A9%D7%91%22%D7%A5)/%D7%97%D7%9C%D7%A7_%D7%90/%D7%A7%D7%9E%D7%96), which cites the Gemara in the name of the unqualified Rav Nachman. He considers this clear; see Rav Nachman bar Rava’s entry.[^4][^3]

notes.text: Hyman argues for an unqualified Rav Nachman in the marketplace saying while preserving a separate Nachman bar Abba reading in Avodah Zarah. His variant arguments are not a canonical identity merger.

The consulted Rashi on Kiddushin 33a quotes “how many Nachmans” without bar Abba, while the consulted Gemara includes bar Abba. Hyman reports the other exact-edition omissions; this comparison does not establish a canonical identity.
The two linked Gemara passages include bar Abba in different settings. In the marketplace explanation, Rashi quotes “how many Nachmans.” The other edition reports remain Hyman’s.

The Tashbetz quotes the Sheiltot with “how many Nachmans like me stand in the marketplace,” without “bar Abba.” In the consulted [Sheiltot d'Rav Achai Gaon 101:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Sheiltot_d%27Rav_Achai_Gaon.101.1), the saying likewise lacks “bar Abba” and has no “like me.”
